definitions.explanation: Goods or items that have been brought in from overseas. Carries a somewhat old-fashioned connotation of exotic or high-quality Western imports, reflecting historical attitudes toward foreign products.

examples.japanese: これは{舶来|はくらい}の{時計|とけい}だ。
{祖父|そふ}は{舶来|はくらい}のウイスキーを{大切|たいせつ}にしていた。
examples.english: My grandfather treasured his imported whiskey.

examples.japanese: {明治時代|めいじじだい}には{舶来品|はくらいひん}が{高級品|こうきゅうひん}の{象徴|しょうちょう}だった。
examples.english: In the Meiji era, imported goods were a symbol of luxury.

notes:
Literally "arriving by ship" ({舶|はく} = ocean vessel, {来|らい} = coming), reflecting a time when foreign goods arrived by sea.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {舶来品|はくらいひん} (imported goods)
- {舶来|はくらい}もの (imported items)
- {舶来|はくらい}の{洋酒|ようしゅ} (imported Western liquor)

This word has a distinctly nostalgic or old-fashioned flavor. It was especially common in the Meiji through early Showa periods, when Western imports were rare and prestigious. In modern Japanese, {輸入|ゆにゅう} (import) is the standard neutral term. {舶来|はくらい} is now mainly used to evoke a sense of vintage luxury or in historical contexts.
